newsitem.title: LEBANON: Palestinian offers to sell son to treat father.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian offers to sell son to treat father.

text.p: A Palestinian man in south Lebanon said on Friday he was offering his seven-year-old son for sale for 40 million Lebanese pounds ($25,680) to pay for his father's medical expenses.

Nabil Refaii, 32, told reporters he was offering his son Haitham for sale after failing to get UNRWA, the U.N. agency that cares for Palestinian refugees, to pay his 60-year-old father Ali's kidney dialysis bill.

"As UNRWA was not responding to our demands, this forced me to offer my son for sale to whoever wants him so I can get 40 million pounds, the cost of my father's medical expenses so far," he said in Ain el-Hilweh refugee camp in south Lebanon.

Refaii, who as a labourer earns about 15,000 pounds a day, also appealed to humanitarian agencies to help his father, who he said was in the intensive care unit at a hospital in the nearby port of Sidon.
A south Lebanon prosecutor said that under Lebanese law Refaii could face up to three years jail if convicted of the crime of selling his child.
